# mk8

Accumulator machine inspired by [Human Resource Machine](https://store.steampowered.com/app/375820/Human_Resource_Machine/): `mk7` extended with pointer access, subroutines and extra conditional jumps. One register (`acc`), word-addressed memory (`mem`), a separate return stack and 16-bit words. Every instruction is 2 words: `op a`.

## How to think in mk8

- Everything goes through `acc`: *load*, compute with memory cells, *store*. `load a sub b jn less` reads as "if a < b goto less".
- Constants live in memory: programs start with `lit 0 to 0  lit 1 to 1`, so `add 1` means +1.
- There is no mul/div: multiply by repeated addition, divide by repeated subtraction, halve with `asr 1`.
- Recursion needs a manual data stack: `push s` / `pop s` (or the `push-s`/`pop-s` aliases) save locals around `cal`.
- Aliases make it readable: `load=lda to=sta peek=lpa poke=spa call=cal`, variables as `n=2`.

## Instruction set

| opcode | # | args | semantics | C (c/ci/cd) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HLT` | 0 | 0 | halt the program | yes |
| `IN` | 1 | 0 | acc = read integer from stdin | yes |
| `OUT` | 2 | 0 | write acc to stdout | yes |
| `LDA` | 3 | a | acc = mem[a] | yes |
| `STA` | 4 | a | mem[a] = acc | yes |
| `ADD` | 5 | a | acc += mem[a] | yes |
| `SUB` | 6 | a | acc -= mem[a] | yes |
| `INC` | 7 | a | mem[a] += 1 | yes |
| `DEC` | 8 | a | mem[a] -= 1 | yes |
| `JMP` | 9 | a | jump to a | yes |
| `JZ` | 10 | a | jump to a if acc == 0 | yes |
| `JN` | 11 | a | jump to a if acc < 0 | yes |
| `LIT` | 12 | a | acc = a | yes |
| `CAL` | 13 | a | call subroutine at a (return address on the return stack) | yes |
| `RET` | 14 | 0 | return from subroutine | yes |
| `LPA` | 15 | a | acc = mem[mem[a]] (load via pointer) | yes |
| `SPA` | 16 | a | mem[mem[a]] = acc (store via pointer) | yes |
| `ASR` | 17 | a | acc >>= a (arithmetic shift right by a constant) | yes |
| `NOP` | 18 | a | do nothing (a can mark a label) | yes |
| `PUSH` | 19 | a | mem[a] += 1; mem[mem[a]] = acc (a = stack pointer cell) | yes |
| `POP` | 20 | a | acc = mem[mem[a]]; mem[a] -= 1 | yes |
| `JP` | 21 | a | jump to a if acc > 0 | yes |
| `JZP` | 22 | a | jump to a if acc >= 0 | yes |
| `JZN` | 23 | a | jump to a if acc <= 0 | yes |
| `LPAO` | 24 | a b | acc = mem[mem[a]+b] (Nim only, 3 words) | no |
| `SPAO` | 25 | a b | mem[mem[a]+b] = acc (Nim only, 3 words) | no |

## Implementations

| variant | file | dispatch |
|---|---|---|
| mk8c | [c/mk8c.c](../c/mk8c.c) | switch |
| mk8ci | [c/mk8ci.c](../c/mk8ci.c) | token threading (`goto *labels[op]`, called "indirect" in README) |
| mk8cd | [c/mk8cd.c](../c/mk8cd.c) | direct threading (code translated to label addresses) |
| mk8 (Nim) | [nim/mk8.nim](../nim/mk8.nim) | case statement |
| mk8 (JS) | [js/mk8.js](../js/mk8.js) | switch; also in the browser: [web/index.html](../web/index.html) |

```
make bin                                   # builds bin/mk8c bin/mk8ci bin/mk8cd (and bin/mk8_nim if nim is installed)
python3 python/asm.py nim/mk8_opcodes.nim asm/gcd_mk8.asm -f b10 -o build/gcd.b10
echo "1 48 18" | bin/mk8c build/gcd.b10           # -> 6
echo "1 48 18" | bin/mk8c build/gcd.b10 -b 100    # benchmark: time and VM cycles on stderr
```
